newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London led higher by HK bank.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London led higher by HK bank.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were dragged higher by sharp gains in HSBC Holdings, as the stock tracked the UK banking sector up on bid rumours.

The Hang Seng London Reference Index was 78.27 points higher at 14,969 ten minutes after the U.S. opening. As the Dow quickly notched up a 70-point rise, Hong Kong stocks rose to their best levels of the day.
The main feature was HSBC Holdings, dealers said.
"HongKong Bank took its lead from the UK market, where the banking sector is up strongly on takeover rumours," one said. "Most of the rest of the market is trading around the Hong Kong close."
HSBC was up HK$3 from its close in Hong Kong.
Traders said sentiment had improved as U.S. stocks bounced back from the Dow's second biggest single-day points loss in history on Monday. A firmer bond market was also lending support, they said.
